<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard AUR package for wezterm-git, a Git-based development version of the WezTerm terminal emulator. It fetches the source from the official GitHub repository using a git+ssh URL, which is expected for -git packages. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is appropriate here because the source is a VCS checkout, and checksums are not applicable.

The build process uses standard Rust tooling (`cargo build`, `cargo test`) with appropriate flags like `--frozen` and `--locked` to ensure reproducibility and avoid network access during build. Submodules are initialized with `git submodule update --init --recursive --depth=1`, which is normal for projects that use submodules. A `sed` command modifies a Cargo.toml file to remove `"vendored-fonts"`, which is a known packaging adjustment to avoid bundling fonts and instead rely on system fonts — a common practice in Linux distributions.

All installed files are built from the source or are static assets included in the upstream repository (icons, desktop files, shell completions, etc.). No network requests, downloads, or executions from external sources occur in the build or package functions. The use of `cargo fetch --locked` in `prepare()` is safe as it only prefetches dependencies defined in the locked manifest.

There are no signs of obfuscation, unauthorized data exfiltration, or execution of untrusted code. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices for a Rust-based -git package and poses no security risk.
</details>
